analysis.title: GlobalFoundries Inc. (GFS): Datacenter strength offsets smartphone and automotive headwinds, with improving gross margin execution
key_insights: GS expects GFS to be range bound higher after a solid 3Q26 with 4Q guidance in line with the Street. Investor expectations were balanced going in: optimism on the SiPh/CPO ramp and quantum, offset by concerns about mobile and automotive.
Management raised its 2026 Datacenter/Comms Infrastructure growth outlook to 60%-70% from 50%-60%, led by silicon photonics and SiGe.
Management pulled its silicon photonics $1bn run-rate revenue target forward to exiting CY27 from CY28. Silicon photonics revenue is expected to more than double in 2026.
3Q26 revenue was $1.90bn, in line with GS at $1.90bn and the Street (Visible Alpha) at $1.89bn. Gross margin of 31.4% was in line with GS at 31.2% and above the Street at 30.6%.
3Q26 Non-IFRS EPS was $0.53 against GS at $0.55 and the Street at $0.51.

Segment revenue vs GS: Home and Industrial IoT $384mn was well above GS at $364mn. Automotive $368mn was below GS at $383mn and the Street at $377mn. Smart Mobile Devices $611mn, Datacenter/Comms Infrastructure $316mn and Technology Services $220mn were in line.

GFS announced a joint venture with the US and Japanese governments to expand its Malta, New York facility by up to 1.8mn wafers per year over time, with $21bn of total capital expected under a multi-year initiative. The model is an SPV co-owned by the two governments, with GF as operator recognizing incremental margin and revenue.

Gross margin (ex-SBC) rose 540 bps y/y to 31.4%, driven by mix shift toward datacenter and automotive, operational improvements, footprint optimization and higher utilization. 4Q guidance of 31.5% is ahead of the company's target of 30% by end of 2026, and GS believes margins can keep expanding.
4Q26 guidance: revenue $2.00bn at the midpoint (GS $1.99bn, Street $2.00bn), gross margin 31.5% (GS 31.7%, Street 31.2%), Non-IFRS EPS $0.59 (GS $0.64, Street $0.57).
GS CY26-28 EPS estimates are essentially unchanged. GS cut its 12-month price target to $62 from $70, on 22x P/E (down from 25x because of lower peer multiples) applied to normalized EPS of $2.80.

GS keeps a Neutral rating. It sees Datacenter/Comms Infrastructure as an idiosyncratic growth engine, but expects near-term pricing and inventory pressure in Smart Mobile Devices, Consumer/IoT and Automotive. It would turn more constructive on evidence of broad-based revenue upside supporting higher earnings power.

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut to $62 from $70 on a 22x P/E (from 25x on lower peer multiples) applied to normalized EPS of $2.80. Rating stays Neutral after an in-line quarter and guidance.

sector_views.rationale: Datacenter/Comms Infrastructure is a growth driver for GFS, but smartphone, consumer/IoT and automotive face pricing and inventory pressure.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 (reported 11/4): revenue $1.90bn vs GS $1.90bn and Street (Visible Alpha) $1.89bn. Revenue was up 12.5% y/y and 6.3% q/q.
3Q26 reported gross margin 31.4% vs GS 31.2% and Street 30.6%. Operating margin 17.9% vs GS 16.9% and Street 16.8%.
3Q26 reported Non-IFRS EPS $0.53 vs GS estimate $0.55 and Street estimate $0.51.

3Q26 segment revenue (reported): Smart Mobile Devices $611mn (GS $612mn, Street $614mn), Datacenter/Comms Infrastructure $316mn (GS $319mn, Street $314mn), Home and Industrial IoT $384mn (GS $364mn, Street $362mn), Automotive $368mn (GS $383mn, Street $377mn), Non-Wafer and Corporate Other $220mn (GS $221mn, Street $220mn).

4Q26 company guidance: revenue midpoint $2.00bn (range $1.975bn-$2.025bn), gross margin 31.5% midpoint, operating margin 19.8% midpoint, Non-IFRS EPS $0.59 midpoint (range $0.54-$0.64). GS estimates are revenue $1.99bn, EPS $0.64. Street estimates are revenue $2.00bn, EPS $0.57.

GS estimates, new vs old: 2026E revenue $7,330mn (old $7,309mn) and Non-IFRS EPS $2.03 (old $2.05). 2027E revenue $8,234mn (old $8,133mn) and EPS $2.70 (unchanged). 2028E revenue $9,166mn (old $9,071mn) and EPS $3.30 (unchanged).

tension_points.bull_case: Datacenter/Comms Infrastructure is an idiosyncratic growth engine. Management raised its 2026 growth outlook to 60%-70%, pulled the silicon photonics $1bn run-rate target forward a year, and gross margin is expanding on mix and utilization.
tension_points.bear_case: GS expects near-term pricing and inventory pressure in Smart Mobile Devices, Consumer/IoT and Automotive. Automotive revenue missed GS and the Street in 3Q26.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS says it could be more constructive if it sees evidence of broad-based revenue upside that supports significantly higher earnings power.
